To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a continuous-space model can be derived from a discrete-state model, (2) a discrete-state model can be derived by a systematic procedure from a continuous-space model, (3) the discrete-state model can then be simulated stochastically and the results compared with those of the continuous-space model, and (4) this approach is a useful way to check the correctness of the discrete-state model.
the use of numerical differentiation to obtain a continuous-space model of a process algebra model can lead to incorrect results.

the use of implicit differentiation formulae in the numerical evaluation of biochemical signalling pathway models can lead to misleading results and that, in order to avoid this, the use of approximate stochastic simulation should be employed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational methods that allow us to model and simulate biochemical signalling pathways and to analyse the results of these simulations.
the development of a framework for the analysis and simulation of biochemical reaction networks that allows for a seamless integration of discrete and continuous representations.

the use of both stochastic and deterministic methods for modelling biochemical pathways and we are particularly interested in the automatic generation of models from a process-algebraic representation of the system under study.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of numerical differentiation is not recommended for the analysis of biochemical pathways.

, for the purposes of modelling the signalling pathways of interest here, the stochastic method is more appropriate than the deterministic method, although it is more expensive in terms of computation time.
the use of both numerical and stochastic simulation methods is essential for the analysis of signalling pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of both continuous-space and stochastic simulation methods are essential in the analysis of biochemical signalling pathways and that the use of the continuous-space method should be used with great care.
the combination of continuous and discrete-state modelling techniques is a powerful approach to understanding the behaviour of biochemical signalling pathways.

we have shown that the use of both continuous and discrete state models is important to the understanding and analysis of signalling pathways and that the use of stochastic simulation can be used to complement the use of numerical integration techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a hybrid modelling approach, where both continuous and discrete representations of the same model are used, can be a valuable approach for understanding the behaviour of signalling pathways.
a combination of continuous and discrete-state methods is needed to obtain a more accurate and reliable representation of biochemical signalling pathways.
both continuous- and discrete-state representations are needed in order to gain confidence in the model.
